# SC4SAP Program → User Manual

Reads one ABAP program via MCP and writes the manual a business user follows to run it: which screen to open, what to enter, which button to press, what the result means and what to do when a message appears. Output is **one HTML file** — a scrolling web document with a contents sidebar on screen, and one scenario step per A4 landscape page when printed or saved as PDF.

<Purpose>
Key users and help desks need a task-oriented manual, not a specification. `program-to-spec` describes what the program does for consultants and developers; this skill describes **how a user does their job with it**, step by step, on pictures of the real screens.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Multi-phase skill. Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md): `auto` (default) uses the model in `Agent_Composition` below; `user-defined` asks the user Opus / Sonnet / Haiku (recommended one first) before each dispatch group.</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** One program, one module consultant for business context — no cross-module synthesis.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- User says "user manual", "manual for this program", "매뉴얼 만들어줘", "사용자 매뉴얼", "현업 매뉴얼", "操作マニュアル", "training material for <program>"
- Go-live / hypercare: key users need step-by-step instructions for a custom report or transaction
- Help-desk handover: messages and what to do about them must be written down
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- User wants a functional / technical specification → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- User wants a process document spanning a whole package → `/sc4sap:package-to-process`
- The object has no user interface (class, FM, CDS, RAP without UI) — there is nothing to click through; suggest `program-to-spec`
- The program does not exist yet
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Session_Trust_Bootstrap>
**MANDATORY — Step 0, before any MCP call or user interaction.** Invoke `/sc4sap:trust-session` with `parent_skill=sc4sap:program-to-manual`. Skip silently if `.sc4sap/session-trust.log` has a line within the last 24h. Full spec: [`../trust-session/SKILL.md`](../trust-session/SKILL.md).
</Session_Trust_Bootstrap>

<Decisions_Fixed>
These were settled when the skill was designed — do not ask the user about them again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Unit | One program = one manual (all its screens, options and follow-up screens) |
| Format | One self-contained `.html`; web document on screen, print CSS = one step per A4 landscape page |
| Editing | The page has a built-in edit mode (no install, no network): edit text, reorder / duplicate / delete steps, add / delete / drag callouts, add / delete rows of the field, message and glossary tables, paste real screenshots, redraw the process flow (drag shapes, draw / reconnect arrows, add / delete steps, change shape kind and text), undo, autosave, save a copy. The copy embeds its manual.json and is imported back (workflow Step 0) |
| Screens | Drawn from source with the `program-to-spec` renderer (selection screen, output ALV, **every follow-up screen and popup the scenarios pass through**), inlined as SVG |
| Callouts | Numbered marks on the drawn screen, tied to screen elements by anchor key; the same numbers head the step's instruction list |
| Body structure | By usage scenario ("to do X") — radio options, execution modes and buttons that start a distinct task each become a scenario |
| Business context | Module consultant drafts it; low-confidence items go to a 1–3 question interview |
| Check points | Derived from source validations, mandatory fields, confirmation popups and irreversible processing (posting, sending); business rules added from the interview |
| Extra sections | Field reference (selection + output) and Messages & actions |
| Front / back matter | Cover, revision history (automatic), glossary |
| Language | One language per manual file (ko / en / ja); mixed prose is rejected by the build check. An English companion is always built as well (Step 8) unless the manual language is English or the user opts out |
| Cover / footer | Author, team, company, confidentiality notice from the active profile's `config.json` → `manual`, asked once |
| Location | `<artifact-base>/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<version>-<lang>.html` (artifact base per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md)) |
</Decisions_Fixed>

<Workflow_Steps>
**MUST read [`workflow-steps.md`](workflow-steps.md)** and execute its steps in order whenever this skill runs.
</Workflow_Steps>

<Manual_Schema>
**MUST read [`manual-schema.md`](manual-schema.md)** before writing `manual.json` (Step 5) — JSON shape, anchor keys, callout and check-point rules. The screen specs inside it follow [`../program-to-spec/selection-schema.md`](../program-to-spec/selection-schema.md) and [`../program-to-spec/alv-buttons-schema.md`](../program-to-spec/alv-buttons-schema.md).
</Manual_Schema>

<Agent_Composition>
The main thread follows the session model (`model: inherit`); each dispatch carries its own model. Every `subagent_type` uses the plugin prefix `sc4sap:`.

- **Main thread** — Steps 0–2 and 6–8: interview, config, MCP inventory, build, review loop, English build.
- **`sc4sap:sap-analyst` × 1 (Opus, frontmatter)** — Step 3: scenarios, steps, screens per step, check points with their source, fields, messages. Returns text; never writes files.
- **`sc4sap:sap-<module>-consultant` × 1 (frontmatter model)** — Step 3, in parallel with the analyst: purpose, background, business rules, users, glossary, and the user action for each message. Marks each claim it inferred rather than read.
- **`sc4sap:sap-writer` × 2 (`model: "sonnet"` override)** — Step 5: writes `manual.json` with the `Write` tool; Step 8: translates the final one into the English companion. User-facing instructional prose needs Sonnet; Haiku drifts into spec language.
</Agent_Composition>

<Output_Format>
```
Manual generated: ZMMR_GR_3PL  v1.0 · ko
Scenarios: 3 · Steps: 8 · Screens drawn: 4 (selection, 0100, 0200 popup, 0300)
Callouts: 21 (all anchored) · Check points: 7 · Messages: 9 · Glossary: 6
File: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-v1.0-ko.html
English: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-v1.0-en.html
History: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-ko.history.json · ZMMR_GR_3PL-en.history.json

To be confirmed (shown with a badge in the manual): 1
Next: "add a scenario", "Japanese version", "new version after the change in TR <n>", "import the edited HTML"
```
</Output_Format>

<MCP_Tools_Used>
- `SearchObject`, `GetObjectInfo`, `GetTransaction`
- `GetProgFullCode`, `GetIncludesList`, `GetInclude`
- `GetScreensList`, `GetScreen`, `GetGuiStatusList`, `GetGuiStatus`, `GetTextElement` (`language: "E"` first)
- `GetSqlQuery` — T100 message texts only (see Data_Extraction_Safety)
- `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` (optional, for validation branches)
</MCP_Tools_Used>

<Data_Extraction_Safety>
Same rule as `program-to-spec`: only source, DDIC metadata and screen definitions are read — never `GetTableContents`. The one exception is **T100** through `GetSqlQuery` with explicit fields (`ARBGB, MSGNR, TEXT`), `SPRSL` = the manual language (fall back to `'E'`) and only the message classes / numbers the source uses; the normal approval prompt applies. **Sample values in screen mockups are invented** (`4500000015`, `KR01`, `100234`) — never business data, never real customer, vendor or company names. Refuse requests to fill mockups with real rows and say why.
</Data_Extraction_Safety>

<Related_Skills>
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — the specification of the same program (shares the screen renderer and schemas)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — process view across a package
- `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` — CBO inventory that enriches the business context
</Related_Skills>

content.text:
Business Rule과 시나리오별 Check Points에도 편집 모드에서 항목을 추가하고 삭제하는 기능을 넣었습니다. 표에 있는 행 추가/삭제와 같은 방식입니다. 브라우저에서 추가, 삭제, 저장, 되돌리기를 확인했고 테스트는 365개 모두 통과합니다.

**사용법 ([편집] 모드)**
- 각 항목 끝에 `＋`(아래에 추가)와 `✕`(삭제) 버튼이 생깁니다. 목록 맨 아래에는 `＋ 항목 추가` 버튼이 있습니다.
- 새 항목은 바로 입력할 수 있는 상태로 열리고, 굵게·강조·목록 서식도 다른 칸처럼 쓸 수 있습니다. Ctrl+Z로 되돌릴 수 있습니다.
- **목록이 비어 있어도 추가할 수 있습니다.** Check Points가 없는 시나리오나 Business Rule이 없는 매뉴얼은 평소에는 그 칸이 숨겨져 있다가, 편집 모드에서만 나타나 첫 항목을 넣을 수 있습니다.
- **저장할 때 내용이 빈 항목은 자동으로 빠집니다.** 항목을 모두 지우면 그 칸은 다시 숨겨집니다.
- 기존 Check Point의 출처 표시(예: `(FORM REFINE_DATA …)`)는 글자를 고쳐도 그대로 남습니다. 새로 추가한 항목에는 출처가 붙지 않습니다.
- "확인 필요" 표시가 붙은 Business Rule은 문구를 고쳐도 그 표시가 계속 따라갑니다.

`--import`로 매뉴얼 데이터에 반영하는 방식은 기존과 같습니다. 바뀐 파일은 `build-manual.mjs`, `manual-editor.mjs`, `program-to-manual/SKILL.md`와 테스트 하나이고, 커밋 없이 프로젝트 소스에만 반영했습니다.

**확인해 주실 것**
- **이미 만든 매뉴얼에는 이 기능이 없습니다.** 오늘 만든 `ZSDM24710-v1.0-ko.html`과 `-en.html`은 이전 빌더로 만들었으니, 같은 버전으로 다시 빌드해야 버튼이 보입니다. 다시 빌드할까요?
- 시험에 쓴 브라우저 탭에 저장하지 않은 편집이 남아 있어 닫으면 확인창이 뜰 수 있습니다. 직접 닫아 주세요.

**함께 넣으면 좋을 기능 (제안)**
1. **항목 순서 바꾸기(▲▼):** 지금은 추가와 삭제만 됩니다. 스텝 이동 버튼처럼 항목 위·아래 이동을 붙이면 순서를 고칠 수 있습니다.
2. **Check Point를 다른 시나리오로 옮기기:** 지금은 한쪽에서 지우고 다른 쪽에 다시 써야 합니다.
3. **용어집의 용어를 자동 링크:** Business Rule이나 Check Point에 용어집에 있는 용어가 나오면 그 설명으로 연결합니다.

필요한 것을 골라 주시면 이어서 하겠습니다. 1번은 작업량이 작습니다.

---
name: program-to-manual
description: Write an end-user manual (one self-contained HTML file) for one ABAP program — scenario-by-scenario steps drawn on selection / ALV / popup screen mockups with numbered callouts, check points derived from the source validations, field reference, messages with actions, glossary and revision history. # SC4SAP Program → User Manual

Reads one ABAP program via MCP and writes the manual a business user follows to run it: which screen to open, what to enter, which button to press, what the result means and what to do when a message appears. Output is **one HTML file** — a scrolling web document with a contents sidebar on screen, and one scenario step per A4 landscape page when printed or saved as PDF.

<Purpose>
Key users and help desks need a task-oriented manual, not a specification. `program-to-spec` describes what the program does for consultants and developers; this skill describes **how a user does their job with it**, step by step, on pictures of the real screens.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Multi-phase skill. Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md): `auto` (default) uses the model in `Agent_Composition` below; `user-defined` asks the user Opus / Sonnet / Haiku (recommended one first) before each dispatch group.</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** One program, one module consultant for business context — no cross-module synthesis.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- User says "user manual", "manual for this program", "매뉴얼 만들어줘", "사용자 매뉴얼", "현업 매뉴얼", "操作マニュアル", "training material for <program>"
- Go-live / hypercare: key users need step-by-step instructions for a custom report or transaction
- Help-desk handover: messages and what to do about them must be written down
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- User wants a functional / technical specification → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- User wants a process document spanning a whole package → `/sc4sap:package-to-process`
- The object has no user interface (class, FM, CDS, RAP without UI) — there is nothing to click through; suggest `program-to-spec`
- The program does not exist yet
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Session_Trust_Bootstrap>
**MANDATORY — Step 0, before any MCP call or user interaction.** Invoke `/sc4sap:trust-session` with `parent_skill=sc4sap:program-to-manual`. Skip silently if `.sc4sap/session-trust.log` has a line within the last 24h. Full spec: [`../trust-session/SKILL.md`](../trust-session/SKILL.md).
</Session_Trust_Bootstrap>

# SC4SAP Program → User Manual

Reads one ABAP program via MCP and writes the manual a business user follows to run it: which screen to open, what to enter, which button to press, what the result means and what to do when a message appears. 요청하신 기능과 1~3번 제안을 모두 넣었고, 한글판과 영문판 매뉴얼을 같은 v1.0으로 다시 빌드했습니다. 빌드 경고는 0건이고, 테스트 366개(새 테스트 포함)가 모두 통과했습니다. 브라우저에서도 동작을 확인했습니다.
- `.sc4sap/work/HKT-DEV/manuals/ZSDM24710-v1.0-ko.html`
- `.sc4sap/work/HKT-DEV/manuals/ZSDM24710-v1.0-en.html`

**편집 모드에서 새로 되는 것**

| 대상 | 기능 |
|---|---|
| 스텝 설명 (예: 2-1의 "If the sales organization…") | 한 줄이 한 항목입니다. 각 줄 끝의 ▲▼＋✕로 순서를 바꾸고 추가·삭제하며, 아래 `＋ 설명 줄 추가` 버튼도 있습니다 |
| 번호 콜아웃의 상세 (예: 2-2 ①의 "Do not insert…") | 같은 ▲▼＋✕ 버튼이 있고, 각 번호 아래 `＋ 상세 추가` 버튼으로 상세가 없던 번호에도 넣을 수 있습니다 |
| Result | 비어 있으면 편집 모드에서 "결과를 입력하세요"가 흐리게 보이고, 클릭해서 바로 쓸 수 있습니다 |
| Business Rule, Check Points (제안 1) | ＋✕에 더해 ▲▼로 순서를 바꿀 수 있습니다 |
| Check Point 이동 (제안 2) | ⇄ 버튼으로 다른 시나리오 목록을 고르면 그 시나리오의 Check Points 맨 끝으로 옮겨집니다 |
| 용어집 자동 링크 (제안 3) | 본문에 나오는 용어집 용어에 점선 밑줄이 생깁니다. 마우스를 올리면 뜻이 보이고, 클릭하면 용어집의 해당 행으로 이동합니다. 스텝, Check Points 상자, 섹션마다 첫 번째로 나오는 곳에만 붙어서 이 매뉴얼에서는 73곳입니다. 편집을 끝내면 고친 글과 용어집을 기준으로 다시 붙습니다 |

- 새로 만든 빈 줄에는 "내용을 입력하세요"가 흐리게 보입니다.
- 모든 동작은 Ctrl+Z로 되돌릴 수 있습니다.
- 내용이 빈 항목은 저장할 때 빠집니다.
- 스텝 설명은 저장할 때 지금처럼 문자열 하나로 합쳐 저장하므로, `--import`와 다시 빌드하는 흐름은 그대로입니다.

**확인해 주실 것**
- 다시 빌드하면서 두 파일은 덮어썼습니다. 오늘 만든 파일이라 다른 사용자 편집은 없었습니다.
- `ZSDM24710-v1.0-ko 1.html`(예전 복사본)에는 새 기능이 없습니다.
- 바뀐 파일은 `build-manual.mjs`, `manual-editor.mjs`, `manual-page.mjs`, `program-to-manual/SKILL.md`, 테스트 파일입니다. 흐름도 편집기와 함께 아직 커밋하지 않았고, 테스트가 끝나면 동기화하겠습니다.

content.text:
영문판은 따로 적용할 것이 없습니다. 지금 있는 영문판은 오늘 만든 `ZSDM24710-v1.0-en.html` 하나뿐이고, 이 파일은 10:29에 새 기능을 넣어 다시 빌드한 버전입니다. 목록 편집과 용어집 링크 코드가 들어 있는 것도 확인했습니다.

**새 기능이 안 보이면**
- 브라우저에서 그 파일을 새로고침(Ctrl+F5)해 주세요. 다시 빌드하기 전에 열어 둔 탭이면 예전 화면이 그대로 남아 있습니다.
- 위쪽에 "저장하지 않은 편집이 있습니다 [이어서 편집] [버리기]" 안내가 뜨면 **[버리기]**를 눌러 주세요. 그 임시저장본은 다시 빌드하기 전 페이지라서, [이어서 편집]을 누르면 새 기능이 없는 예전 화면이 열립니다.

**찾다가 확인한 것**
바탕화면에 9월 30일에 편집해 저장한 `ZSDM24710-v1.0-ko-edited.html`이 있습니다. 이 편집은 아직 매뉴얼 데이터에 반영되지 않아서, 오늘 만든 한글판과 영문판 모두 이 편집이 빠져 있습니다.
- 바뀐 곳은 시나리오 2-4의 3번째 스텝입니다. 그림 대신 실제 캡처(1200×1200)를 넣었고, 번호 설명(콜아웃)도 고쳤습니다.
- 다른 시나리오와 스텝 수는 그대로입니다.

혹시 "예전 버전"이 이 파일을 말씀하신 것이라면, 이 편집을 가져와 한글판과 영문판 둘 다 v1.1로 다시 만들 수 있습니다.
- 캡처 이미지는 두 언어에 똑같이 들어갑니다.
- 고친 번호 설명은 영문판용으로 번역합니다.

진행할까요?

---
name: program-to-manual
description: Write an end-user manual (one self-contained HTML file) for one ABAP program — scenario-by-scenario steps drawn on selection / ALV / popup screen mockups with numbered callouts, check points derived from the source validations, field reference, messages with actions, glossary and revision history. Web document on screen, one step per A4 landscape page in print.
model: inherit
---

# SC4SAP Program → User Manual

Reads one ABAP program via MCP and writes the manual a business user follows to run it: which screen to open, what to enter, which button to press, what the result means and what to do when a message appears. Output is **one HTML file** — a scrolling web document with a contents sidebar on screen, and one scenario step per A4 landscape page when printed or saved as PDF.

<Purpose>
Key users and help desks need a task-oriented manual, not a specification. `program-to-spec` describes what the program does for consultants and developers; this skill describes **how a user does their job with it**, step by step, on pictures of the real screens.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Multi-phase skill. Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md): `auto` (default) uses the model in `Agent_Composition` below; `user-defined` asks the user Opus / Sonnet / Haiku (recommended one first) before each dispatch group.</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** One program, one module consultant for business context — no cross-module synthesis.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- User says "user manual", "manual for this program", "매뉴얼 만들어줘", "사용자 매뉴얼", "현업 매뉴얼", "操作マニュアル", "training material for <program>"
- Go-live / hypercare: key users need step-by-step instructions for a custom report or transaction
- Help-desk handover: messages and what to do about them must be written down
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- User wants a functional / technical specification → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- User wants a process document spanning a whole package → `/sc4sap:package-to-process`
- The object has no user interface (class, FM, CDS, RAP without UI) — there is nothing to click through; suggest `program-to-spec`
- The program does not exist yet
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Session_Trust_Bootstrap>
**MANDATORY — Step 0, before any MCP call or user interaction.** Invoke `/sc4sap:trust-session` with `parent_skill=sc4sap:program-to-manual`. Skip silently if `.sc4sap/session-trust.log` has a line within the last 24h. Full spec: [`../trust-session/SKILL.md`](../trust-session/SKILL.md).
</Session_Trust_Bootstrap>

<Decisions_Fixed>
These were settled when the skill was designed — do not ask the user about them again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Unit | One program = one manual (all its screens, options and follow-up screens) |
| Format | One self-contained `.html`; web document on screen, print CSS = one step per A4 landscape page |
| Editing | The page has a built-in edit mode (no install, no network): edit text, reorder / duplicate / delete steps, add / delete / drag callouts, add / delete rows of the field, message and glossary tables; add / delete / reorder items of the business rules, each scenario's check points (⇄ moves one to another scenario), step note lines and callout details; fill an empty result, paste real screenshots, redraw the process flow (drag shapes, draw / reconnect arrows, add / delete steps, change shape kind and text), undo, autosave, save a copy. The copy embeds its manual.json and is imported back (workflow Step 0) |
| Glossary links | Glossary terms in the prose link to their glossary row (dotted underline, meaning as tooltip) — once per step / check-point box / section, re-linked when edit mode ends |
| Screens | Drawn from source with the `program-to-spec` renderer (selection screen, output ALV, **every follow-up screen and popup the scenarios pass through**), inlined as SVG |
| Callouts | Numbered marks on the drawn screen, tied to screen elements by anchor key; the same numbers head the step's instruction list |
| Body structure | By usage scenario ("to do X") — radio options, execution modes and buttons that start a distinct task each become a scenario |
| Business context | Module consultant drafts it; low-confidence items go to a 1–3 question interview |
| Check points | Derived from source validations, mandatory fields, confirmation popups and irreversible processing (posting, sending); business rules added from the interview |
| Extra sections | Field reference (selection + output) and Messages & actions |
| Front / back matter | Cover, revision history (automatic), glossary |
| Language | One language per manual file (ko / en / ja); mixed prose is rejected by the build check. An English companion is always built as well (Step 8) unless the manual language is English or the user opts out |
| Cover / footer | Author, team, company, confidentiality notice from the active profile's `config.json` → `manual`, asked once |
| Location | `<artifact-base>/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<version>-<lang>.html` (artifact base per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md)) |
</Decisions_Fixed>

<Workflow_Steps>
**MUST read [`workflow-steps.md`](workflow-steps.md)** and execute its steps in order whenever this skill runs.
</Workflow_Steps>

<Manual_Schema>
**MUST read [`manual-schema.md`](manual-schema.md)** before writing `manual.json` (Step 5) — JSON shape, anchor keys, callout and check-point rules. The screen specs inside it follow [`../program-to-spec/selection-schema.md`](../program-to-spec/selection-schema.md) and [`../program-to-spec/alv-buttons-schema.md`](../program-to-spec/alv-buttons-schema.md).
</Manual_Schema>

<Agent_Composition>
The main thread follows the session model (`model: inherit`); each dispatch carries its own model. Every `subagent_type` uses the plugin prefix `sc4sap:`.

- **Main thread** — Steps 0–2 and 6–8: interview, config, MCP inventory, build, review loop, English build.
- **`sc4sap:sap-analyst` × 1 (Opus, frontmatter)** — Step 3: scenarios, steps, screens per step, check points with their source, fields, messages. Returns text; never writes files.
- **`sc4sap:sap-<module>-consultant` × 1 (frontmatter model)** — Step 3, in parallel with the analyst: purpose, background, business rules, users, glossary, and the user action for each message. Marks each claim it inferred rather than read.
- **`sc4sap:sap-writer` × 2 (`model: "sonnet"` override)** — Step 5: writes `manual.json` with the `Write` tool; Step 8: translates the final one into the English companion. User-facing instructional prose needs Sonnet; Haiku drifts into spec language.
</Agent_Composition>

<Output_Format>
```
Manual generated: ZMMR_GR_3PL  v1.0 · ko
Scenarios: 3 · Steps: 8 · Screens drawn: 4 (selection, 0100, 0200 popup, 0300)
Callouts: 21 (all anchored) · Check points: 7 · Messages: 9 · Glossary: 6
File: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-v1.0-ko.html
English: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-v1.0-en.html
History: .sc4sap/work/DEV/manuals/ZMMR_GR_3PL-ko.history.json · ZMMR_GR_3PL-en.history.json

To be confirmed (shown with a badge in the manual): 1
Next: "add a scenario", "Japanese version", "new version after the change in TR <n>", "import the edited HTML"
```
</Output_Format>

<MCP_Tools_Used>
- `SearchObject`, `GetObjectInfo`, `GetTransaction`
- `GetProgFullCode`, `GetIncludesList`, `GetInclude`
- `GetScreensList`, `GetScreen`, `GetGuiStatusList`, `GetGuiStatus`, `GetTextElement` (`language: "E"` first)
- `GetSqlQuery` — T100 message texts only (see Data_Extraction_Safety)
- `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` (optional, for validation branches)
</MCP_Tools_Used>

<Data_Extraction_Safety>
Same rule as `program-to-spec`: only source, DDIC metadata and screen definitions are read — never `GetTableContents`. The one exception is **T100** through `GetSqlQuery` with explicit fields (`ARBGB, MSGNR, TEXT`), `SPRSL` = the manual language (fall back to `'E'`) and only the message classes / numbers the source uses; the normal approval prompt applies. **Sample values in screen mockups are invented** (`4500000015`, `KR01`, `100234`) — never business data, never real customer, vendor or company names. Refuse requests to fill mockups with real rows and say why.
</Data_Extraction_Safety>

<Related_Skills>
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — the specification of the same program (shares the screen renderer and schemas)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — process view across a package
- `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` — CBO inventory that enriches the business context
</Related_Skills>

content.text:
메시지 코드에도 링크를 넣었습니다. 예를 들어 본문의 `E07`을 클릭하면 "오류 메시지 및 조치" 표의 E07 행으로 이동합니다. 한글판과 영문판을 같은 v1.0으로 다시 빌드했고(경고 0건), 테스트 366개가 모두 통과했습니다.

**동작 방식**
- 메시지 표에 있는 코드(E01~E18, Q01 등)를 읽어서, 본문, 콜아웃, 스텝 설명, Business Rule, Check Points에 나오는 같은 코드를 링크로 바꿉니다.
- Check Point 끝의 출처 표기 `(FORM CREATE_IQ (E07))`에 들어 있는 코드도 링크됩니다.
- 마우스를 올리면 메시지 문구와 조치가 함께 보입니다. 예: "Check Errors. — Nothing was created. Go back with Back (F3), fix the errors…"
- 코드는 짧고 찾아보는 용도라서 용어집과 달리 나올 때마다 링크합니다. 영문판에서는 32곳이 링크됐습니다.
- 용어집 링크(점선 밑줄)와 구분되도록 파란색 굵은 글씨에 점선 밑줄로 표시합니다.
- "엑셀 읽기 오류"처럼 코드 대신 이름으로 적힌 행은 링크하지 않습니다.
- 편집 모드에서 메시지 표나 본문을 고친 뒤 편집을 끝내면 링크가 다시 만들어집니다.

브라우저에서 영문판으로 확인했습니다(2-3의 Check Points에서 E07과 E14 링크와 이동 대상 확인).

**참고**
- 열어 둔 매뉴얼 탭이 있으면 Ctrl+F5로 새로고침해 주세요.
- "저장하지 않은 편집이 있습니다" 안내가 뜨면 **[버리기]**를 눌러 주세요. [이어서 편집]은 다시 빌드하기 전 화면을 엽니다.
- 바탕화면의 `ZSDM24710-v1.0-ko-edited.html`(시나리오 2-4의 3번째 스텝 캡처)은 아직 반영하지 않았습니다. 진행할지 알려 주세요.

// ── Build ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export function buildManual({ manualPath, outDir, sameVersion = false, major = false, cwd = process.cwd(), verbose = true }) {
  const manual = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manualPath, 'utf8'));
  // Screen theme: manual.json "theme", else the profile config "screenTheme", else Signature.
  if (manual.theme == null) manual.theme = readScreenTheme(cwd) ?? undefined;
  const lang = manual.lang || 'ko';
  const program = String(manual.program || 'PROGRAM');
  const dir = outDir || join(resolveArtifactBase(cwd), 'manuals');
  mkdirSync(join(dir, '_src'), { recursive: true });

  const warnings = manualWarnings(manual);
  if (verbose) for (const w of warnings) console.log(`⚠ build-manual: ${w}`);

  const cfg = readManualConfig(cwd);
  const config = { ...cfg.manual, ...(manual.meta || {}) };
  const historyPath = join(dir, `${slug(program)}-${lang}.history.json`);
  const history = existsSync(historyPath) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(historyPath, 'utf8')) : { program, lang, versions: [] };
  const version = nextVersion(history, { sameVersion, major });
  const entry = { version, date: today(), author: config.author || '', note: manual.changeNote || '' };
  const versions = arr(history.versions);
  const previous = versions.at(-1)?.version === version ? versions.at(-2) : versions.at(-1);
  if (verbose && previous && entry.note && previous.note === entry.note) {
    console.log(`⚠ build-manual: changeNote "${entry.note}" repeats v${previous.version}'s note — describe what changed in v${version}`);
  }
  if (versions.at(-1)?.version === version) versions[versions.length - 1] = entry;
  else versions.push(entry);
  history.versions = versions;

  const html = renderManualHtml(manual, { version, date: entry.date, config, history: versions });
  const htmlPath = join(dir, `${slug(program)}-v${version}-${lang}.html`);
  const sourcePath = join(dir, '_src', `${slug(program)}-v${version}-${lang}.manual.json`);
  writeFileSync(htmlPath, html, 'utf8');
  writeFileSync(sourcePath, readFileSync(manualPath, 'utf8'), 'utf8');
  writeFileSync(historyPath, `${JSON.stringify(history, null, 2)}\n`, 'utf8');
  if (verbose && !cfg.found && !manual.meta) console.log('⚠ build-manual: no "manual" block in config.json — cover shows no team / author / company (run manual-config.mjs set)');
  return { html: htmlPath, version, history: historyPath, source: sourcePath, warnings };
}

/**
 * Reads the manual.json a user saved from the page's edit mode (embedded as
 * <script id="manual-source">) and writes it to `outPath`, so the next build keeps the edits.
 */
export function importEditedHtml(htmlPath, outPath) {
  const html = readFileSync(htmlPath, 'utf8');
  const m = /<script type="application\/json" id="manual-source">([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/.exec(html);
  if (!m) throw new Error(`${htmlPath} has no embedded manual source — was it saved from the page's edit mode?`);
  const { manual, version } = JSON.parse(m[1]);
  if (existsSync(outPath)) writeFileSync(`${outPath}.bak`, readFileSync(outPath));
  writeFileSync(outPath, `${JSON.stringify(manual, null, 2)}\n`, 'utf8');
  return { manual: outPath, fromVersion: version, edited: manual.edited || null, backup: existsSync(`${outPath}.bak`) ? `${outPath}.bak` : null };
}

const thisFile = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === thisFile && process.argv[2] === '--import') {
  const [, , , htmlPath, outPath] = process.argv;
  if (!htmlPath || !outPath) {
    console.error('Usage: node build-manual.mjs --import <edited.html> <manual.json to write>');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  try {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(importEditedHtml(resolve(htmlPath), resolve(outPath)), null, 2));
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`build-manual: ${e.message}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
} else if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === thisFile) {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  let manualPath;
  let outDir;
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    const a = args[i];
    if (a === '--out-dir') outDir = args[++i];
    else if (a.startsWith('--out-dir=')) outDir = a.slice('--out-dir='.length);
    else if (!a.startsWith('--')) manualPath = a;
  }
  if (!manualPath || (args.some(a => a.startsWith('--out-dir')) && !outDir)) {
    console.error('Usage: node build-manual.mjs <manual.json> [--out-dir DIR] [--same-version] [--major]');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  try {
    const result = buildManual({
      manualPath: resolve(manualPath),
      outDir: outDir ? resolve(outDir) : undefined,
      sameVersion: args.includes('--same-version'),
      major: args.includes('--major'),
    });
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ ...result, warnings: result.warnings.length }, null, 2));
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`build-manual: ${e.message}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

content.text:
이제 편집 모드에서 [저장]을 누르면 개정 이력이 자동으로 추가됩니다. 버전은 0.1씩 오르고 작성자는 저장할 때 묻습니다. 한글판, 영문판, `ko 1.html` 복사본을 모두 이 기능이 들어간 v1.0으로 다시 빌드했습니다(경고 0건). 테스트 367개(새 테스트 포함)가 모두 통과했습니다.

**저장할 때 동작**
1. "저장 — 개정 이력" 창이 뜨고 새 버전과 오늘 날짜가 표시됩니다(예: `v1.1 · 2026-10-06`).
2. **작성자**는 꼭 입력해야 합니다. 비워 두면 "작성자를 입력하세요"가 나오고 저장되지 않습니다. 한 번 입력하면 다음부터 기본값으로 채워집니다.
3. **변경 내용**은 선택입니다. 비워 두면 "편집 모드에서 내용 수정"으로 기록됩니다.
4. 저장하면 페이지 안에서 다음이 바뀝니다.
   - 개정 이력 표에 새 줄이 추가됩니다.
   - 상단 바, 표지, 인쇄 꼬리말의 버전과 일자가 새 버전으로 바뀝니다.
   - 저장 파일 이름에 새 버전이 들어갑니다(`ZSDM24710-v1.1-ko-edited.html`).

**버전이 오르는 방식**
- 페이지를 열고 처음 저장할 때 새 버전이 하나 생깁니다.
- 같은 페이지에서 다시 저장하면 새 줄을 만들지 않고, 작성자가 미리 채워진 창이 떠서 그 버전의 내용을 고칩니다.
- 저장한 v1.1 파일을 나중에 다시 열어 저장하면 v1.2가 됩니다.

**컨설턴트 쪽 흐름**
- 사용자에게 받은 파일을 `--import`하면, 수정한 내용과 함께 사용자가 남긴 이력도 `history.json`에 들어갑니다.
- 그 뒤 `--same-version`으로 빌드하면 사용자가 적은 버전, 작성자, 일자, 변경 내용이 그대로 유지됩니다.
- 컨설턴트가 추가로 고친 내용은 그다음 버전으로 올라갑니다.
- 스킬 문서(`workflow-steps.md` Step 0)에도 이 순서를 적어 두었습니다.

브라우저에서 확인한 것은 작성자 필수 검사, v1.1 생성, 표와 버전 표시 갱신, 저장 파일명, 같은 세션에서 다시 저장할 때 기존 줄을 고치는 동작입니다. 열어 둔 탭은 Ctrl+F5로 새로고침해 주세요.

name: sc4sap plugin — 3-location sync when patching
description: When patching sc4sap plugin code, keep project source + marketplace + user cache in sync (user is plugin author, publishes from project folder)
type: reference
originSessionId: 624e4d17-84e6-4cca-a52f-34db7cd7ad7e
User authors the sc4sap plugin. When patching plugin code (bridge, scripts, hooks, skills), THREE locations must stay in sync:

1. **Project source (distribution source-of-truth)** — `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/sc4sap/`
   - This is what gets published to the marketplace.
   - All new fixes MUST land here first (for git/CHANGELOG).
2. **Marketplace copy (install-time source)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sc4sap/`
   - What Claude Code ships into the cache when the plugin is enabled/updated.
3. **Cache (runtime)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/`
   - What actually runs. A fresh plugin install copies from marketplace → cache, overwriting ad-hoc patches here.

**Patching workflow**:
- Edit project source first.
- Mirror to marketplace (for install-time correctness).
- Mirror to cache (to take effect in the running session — otherwise user must `/reload-plugins` or restart).
- `diff` all three at the end — they should match exactly.

**Why not just cache?** Cache is blown away on plugin update. Project source drives git + publish; marketplace is the Claude Code-facing source.

**Related**: `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` previously only checked legacy `<project>/.sc4sap/sap.env` and `<plugin>/.sc4sap/sap.env`, missing the multi-profile path (`<project>/.sc4sap/active-profile.txt` → `~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/sap.env`). Patched 2026-04-21 in all three locations to resolve via active-profile first, with legacy paths as fallback.
name: Reference — Claude Code /plugin reads .claude-plugin version fields
description: Claude Code marketplace surfaces the version from .claude-plugin/plugin.json + marketplace.json (3 fields total), NOT package.json. Bump all three at each release or /plugin shows a stale version.
type: reference
originSessionId: d0295105-8a83-493b-9c14-d5e48ffe7fad
**Where Claude Code `/plugin` reads "latest version" from:**

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `version` (1 field)
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → `plugins[0].version` (1 field)
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → root `version` (1 field)

**Not** from `package.json`. `package.json.version` is for npm-side consumption only.

**Cache behavior:**
- Installed plugins live at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/` — keyed by the marketplace version string
- When the marketplace manifest shows a new version, Claude Code auto-downloads into a fresh `<new-version>/` dir
- No manual cache patching needed on version bump — only the .claude-plugin manifests

**Incident (2026-04-24):** All three version fields were stuck at `0.6.5` across the 0.6.6 → 0.6.11 release cycle, so `/plugin` kept reporting 0.6.5 as latest even after package.json moved to 0.6.11. Fixed in PR #40 (commit `baf676b`).

**Automated safeguard added in same PR:** `tests/validation/plugin-structure.test.ts` now cross-checks all three .claude-plugin version fields against `package.json.version`. Future drift fails CI at the `verify · typecheck · test` step.

**How to apply:** At every release, bump `package.json.version` AND all three `.claude-plugin/*.json` version fields together. The new CI test will flag it if you miss, but don't rely on that — do it in one commit.
name: Entire-Checkpoint trailer in every commit
description: When making git commits in sc4sap_project, MUST include `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer to keep entire session tracking intact
type: feedback
originSessionId: 21e03650-294e-4f69-aaef-74c569183474
modified: 2026-09-29T23:29:06.682Z
When creating any `git commit` in `sc4sap_project` (or any repo where `entire` is enabled), the commit message MUST include an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer in the trailer block (next to / below `Co-Authored-By:`).

**Why:** `entire attach <session-id>` only registers checkpoint metadata in entire's DB and prints "Copy to your commit message to attach: Entire-Checkpoint: <id>". It does NOT automatically amend the commit to add the trailer (because last commit may already be pushed). The trailer is the chain mechanism — without it on a commit, entire's session ↔ commit linkage breaks for that commit and every subsequent one in the chain.

**How to apply:**
- Before authoring a commit, run `entire sessions list` (or `entire status`) and grab the active session's `checkpoint <id>` field.
- Append `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` as a trailer line in the commit message, on its own line in the trailer block.
- Reuse the same checkpoint ID for every commit in the same Claude Code session — `entire attach` only mints a new checkpoint when there's no checkpoint registered for the session yet.
- If the project active branch is shared (NO force-push policy) and a commit was already pushed without the trailer, do NOT try to fix via `entire attach` afterwards — it will `git commit --amend` the last commit silently and rewrite hash, forcing a reset-to-origin to recover.

**Real incident (2026-04-26):** Commit 1f4c5bf (program-to-spec PNG path fix) was authored without the trailer despite user having run `entire attach 21e03650...` earlier in the session. Result: trailer-less commit pushed to active/backup/main, and a follow-up `entire attach` silently amended local 1f4c5bf → f7615b7 forcing a hash divergence that had to be reset (force-push blocked by shared-branch policy). Net effect: that commit is permanently un-tracked by entire on origin.

**Safe pattern when the session has no checkpoint yet (worked 2026-09-30):** commit first (unpushed), then `entire attach <session-id> -f` — it amends only that unpushed commit with the trailer and mints the checkpoint; reuse the ID for later commits/merge. Never attach while HEAD is an already-pushed commit.

Quick template for commits in this project:
```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: <fetch via `entire sessions list`>
```

name: Always verify locally before publish / git push / any public action
description: Default to local verification (npm pack + install locally, smoke test) before any destructive or public-facing action like npm publish, git push to main, marketplace release
type: feedback
originSessionId: 44e18665-d223-475a-83dc-c08cd0bfcd54
When offered a choice between "just ship it, unit tests passed" and "verify locally first (npm pack → install → smoke test on real system) then ship", the user **always picks verify-first**.

**Why:** The user is cautious about irreversible public actions (npm publish has ~24h unpublish window, git push to main can't be silently undone, marketplace release affects other users). Unit tests use mocks and may miss real-environment shape mismatches. User explicitly said "무섭다" (it's scary) when a git-push plan was laid out without a verification lap first.

**How to apply:**
- For any flow ending in `npm publish`, `git push`, `gh release`, marketplace release, or similar: insert a local verification step **first** and present it as the default path. Do not ask the user to "pick A or B" if one option is a verify-first path — propose verify-first and confirm.
- Local verification pattern for npm libs: `npm pack` in source → install tarball into the consuming project → rebuild consumer → smoke test in the real target system (e.g. actual SAP ECC) before publishing.
- Local verification pattern for git pushes: confirm branch state + remote state + diff against remote before pushing; for destructive remote ops (force push, branch delete, backup-and-replace), pause and explicitly enumerate what will happen.
- If the user is already stressed (e.g. "무섭다", "걱정된다"), acknowledge briefly and lead with the safer path — don't enumerate multiple options again.

# Changelog

All notable changes to **SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap)** will be documented in this file.
Format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.6.32] — 2026-10-02

### Fixed — `trust-session`: no more permission-rule warning at startup

- Permission rules are aligned with Claude Code's path-rule model: `Read(path)` covers all file-reading tools and `Edit(path)` covers all file-editing tools. trust-session now grants only `Read(.sc4sap/**)`, `Read(sc4sap/**)` and `Edit(.sc4sap/**)` (plus `Agent(*)`).
- The stale `Write(.sc4sap/**)`, `Glob(...)` and `Grep(...)` entries that earlier versions wrote never matched and made Claude Code print a warning at startup. trust-session now removes them automatically; no other rule is touched.

## [0.6.31] — 2026-09-30

### Added — `program-to-manual`: edit the finished manual in the page

- The manual page has an **Edit** button. Key users change the finished manual like a slide deck, with nothing installed and nothing loaded from the network:
  - Click any text to change it. Selecting text shows a small toolbar with bold, highlight (red) and bullet list. The toolbar is Quill 2.0.3 (BSD-3-Clause), inlined from `scripts/manual/third_party/quill-2.0.3/` and mounted only on the field being edited.
  - Move, duplicate and delete steps. Add and delete callouts, and drag a callout number to a better place; a leader line keeps it tied to its frame.
  - Replace a drawn screen with a real screenshot: click the step and press Ctrl+V, or use the button. "Original screen" brings the drawing back.
  - Add and delete rows of the field, message and glossary tables, edit every cell, and switch the ● cells (required, F4) with a click.
  - Undo every change with Ctrl+Z or the Undo button.
  - Edits are kept in the browser (IndexedDB) until saved. Reopening the page offers "Continue editing" or "Discard".
  - A short guide opens the first time and stays available under Help.
- **Save** writes a copy of the page (`…-edited.html`) with the edited `manual.json` embedded. `build-manual.mjs --import <edited.html> <manual.json>` reads it back (the old draft is kept as `.bak`), and workflow Step 0 imports a user-edited copy before anything else, so the next version keeps the users' edits.
- New `manual.json` keys written by the edit mode: step `image` (a pasted screenshot, drawn instead of `screen`), callout `offset` / `pos`, top-level `edited`. Prose markup gains `==highlight==` and `- ` bullet lines.
- The page is about 480 KB instead of about 220 KB, because the editor is inlined.

### Added — `program-to-manual`: Excel worksheet screens

## [0.6.33] — 2026-10-06

### Added — process flows you can redraw in the page (`program-to-manual`, `program-to-spec`)

- The process flow is no longer a fixed picture. In the manual's edit mode, and behind an "✎ Edit flow" button on every flow of a spec HTML (main flow and per-button flows), users:
  - drag shapes to move them;
  - drag one of the four dots on a shape onto another shape to draw an arrow (dropping on empty space makes a new step there), or click an arrow and drag its end to reconnect it;
  - add process / decision / message / start / end steps, change a shape's kind, delete shapes and arrows (Delete key);
  - double-click a shape or arrow to change its text (例 "Yes" / "No" on branches).
- An edited flow is saved as a **free graph** (`"layout": "free"`, every node keeps its `x`, `y`; arrows keep their sides). The build draws it from those positions (`scripts/spec/flow-draw.mjs`, the same code the page runs), so the PNG, the Excel sheet and the HTML show the user's layout. Flows nobody edited keep the automatic layout.
- Manual: the flow is part of the manual's edit mode (undo, autosave, Save, `--import`).
- Spec HTML: `render-md-images.mjs` writes `<flow>.graph.json` next to each flow PNG; `md-to-html.mjs` turns those images into editable figures. Save downloads `…-edited.html`; `node scripts/spec/flow-editor.mjs --import <edited.html> <image-spec.json>` writes only the changed flows back (old file kept as `.bak`).

### Added — `program-to-manual`: more of the manual is editable

- Business rules and each scenario's check points: add, delete and reorder items (▲ ▼ ＋ ✕); ⇄ moves a check point to another scenario. Empty lists stay on the page (hidden outside edit mode) so the first item can be added.
- Step notes: one line per item, with the same ▲ ▼ ＋ ✕ and "Add note line". The note is still saved as one string.
- Callout details: add, delete and reorder, also on callouts that had none.
- An empty result shows a placeholder in edit mode and can be filled in.
- Empty items are dropped on save.

### Added — `program-to-manual`: cross-links and automatic revision history

- Glossary terms in the prose link to their glossary row (dotted underline, meaning as tooltip), once per step, check-point box or section.
- Message codes (`E07`, `Q01`, …) link to their row in *Messages and Actions* wherever they appear, check-point sources included; the tooltip shows the message text.
- Links are rebuilt from the page's own tables when edit mode ends.
- Saving in edit mode records a revision: a dialog asks for the author (remembered for next time) and a change note, and the page adds version +0.1 to the revision history, the top bar, the cover and the file name (`…-v1.1-…-edited.html`). Saving again in the same session updates that entry. `--import` writes it to `<PROGRAM>-<lang>.history.json`; a `--same-version` build keeps the user's author, date and note.

### Changed — `program-to-spec`: English companion by default

- When the spec language is not English, a new Step 6 writes English twins of every selected format (`-en.md`, `-en.html`, `-en.xlsx`) after the review, the way `program-to-manual` already does. Structure, SAP identifiers and flow layouts are kept; only prose and labels are translated. Say "no English version" to skip it.
